clue.text: At first, shopper ridicules maternity dresses

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word shopper

parts.note: to ridicule is to mock; mocks is the verb form matching ridicules

explanation.surface: A shopper laughs at the frumpy maternity wear on the rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocks are loose, roomy garments traditionally worn by expectant mothers.

clue.text: Eat a lot around November

indicators.note: around places the a-lot word on either side of the November letter

parts.note: much means a lot
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone gorges themselves at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to chew steadily and audibly, a way to eat.

clue.text: Romantic clubs with lake mostly exclusive

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
and joins things, as with does
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: elite means select or exclusive

explanation.surface: A dreamy getaway of members-only clubs beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner lit by candles is the classic intimate, romantic setting.

clue.text: Unfortunately rises track pay

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: alas is an expression of regret, meaning unfortunately
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Sadly, rising rail fares eat into one's wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed regular pay for a job.

clue.text: Rock outside broadcast, daughter is backing Dury, perhaps

indicators.note: backing means the pair daughter-plus-is is read backwards

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
Ian Dury, the punk-era singer, is an example of someone called Ian

explanation.surface: A TV crew filming on location as a daughter backs the singer Ian Dury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns D + IS round to make SID; 'perhaps' tells you Dury is just one example of an Ian.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a glassy black volcanic stone, a kind of rock.

clue.text: False vision in choice involving independent California damaging the States

indicators.note: involving means the choice word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an option is a choice
ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A political fantasy about California going it alone and harming America.
explanation.walkthrough: Damaging gives ILL in its adjectival sense of harmful, as in ill effects; the four short pieces are then wrapped by the word for choice.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is something the eye perceives wrongly, a deceptive sight.

clue.text: Team round Biden's path

parts.note: a side is a team
a walk is a regular round, as a postman's walk

explanation.surface: A political team encircles the president.
explanation.walkthrough: Biden's marks the definition as American: pavement in Britain is sidewalk in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidewalk is the American word for a pedestrian pavement beside a road.

clue.text: Follow graduate creed

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone is told to adopt the beliefs of a university graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a set of principles laid down as incontrovertibly true, a creed.

clue.text: Three under obligation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in golf, a score of three strokes under par on a hole
second meaning: a burden one cannot shake off, from the Ancient Mariner

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like three people in debt; in golf an albatross is three under par, and the bird in Coleridge's poem is a heavy burden.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabird's name serves for a golf score beyond an eagle and, figuratively, for a burdensome duty.

clue.text: Flat could literally become flaunted

indicators.note: could literally become says the answer's own letters, taken as an instruction on the word flat, produce the word that follows

parts.note: the word flaunted is what you get by following the answer read as an instruction: UN put in FLAT, then ED

explanation.surface: An apartment could, if you squint, be described as showy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN / IN / FLAT / ED: putting UN inside FLAT gives FLAUNT, and adding ED gives FLAUNTED. 'literally' warns you to treat the letters as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not blown up with air, like a deflated tyre, is flat.

clue.text: Taunt soldier, born next to base

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
B is the abbreviation for born in biographies
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a soldier who was born beside the army base.
explanation.walkthrough: Base is the mathematician's e, the base of natural logarithms, not an army camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a mocking remark; to taunt is to make one.

clue.text: Angry, smart about lost role

indicators.note: about places the chic letters around the reworked role

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart

indicators.note: lost suggests the word role has gone astray and is jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor is cross and stinging after losing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric describes a bad-tempered, irritable temperament, from the old humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: The law destroyed riches

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of the law are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Legal authority has been ruined by money.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is an abundance of money and possessions, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Blue drink vile, no contest about it!

parts.note: tea is a common drink

indicators.note: no tells you to drop the letters for contest from the word vile
about it says the removed contest letters sit around what remains

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: A sour remark that some drink is foul, beyond argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing VIE from VILE leaves L; VIE was wrapped about it, hence 'about it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal is a dark greenish-blue colour, named after the duck.

clue.text: Green plan for community

parts.note: eco- denotes environmentally green
a system is a method or plan

explanation.surface: An environmental scheme drawn up for a local neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology an ecosystem is a community of interacting organisms and their environment.

clue.text: Heard green drink is sweet

indicators.note: heard means the word for green is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: green is slang for money, as is lolly in British slang
pop is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that a green fizzy drink is sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: Green as money (greenbacks) gives LOLLY, British slang for cash, spoken as LOLLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sugary confection on a stick, a type of sweet.

clue.text: Italian team ready for French solve

parts.note: Inter is Inter Milan, the Italian football club
pret is French for ready

explanation.surface: An Italian football side prepared for French opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a puzzle or riddle is to work out its meaning, to solve it.

clue.text: Provided American river crossing with agent for protection

indicators.note: for protection means the agent surrounds the crossing as a guard would

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An American river crossing was guarded by an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A fed is American slang for an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Afforded means gave or supplied, as in afforded an opportunity.

clue.text: Opening almost perfect quantity of food

parts.note: a mouth is an opening

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: full can mean complete or perfect, as in full marks

explanation.surface: An opening offer of nearly the ideal portion of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthful is as much food as fits in the mouth at one time.

clue.text: Examine the empty street

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word the is removed, keeping its ends

parts.note: St is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An inspector checks out the deserted road.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to try it out or check it, which is to examine it.

clue.text: Brief hen to bear weight

indicators.note: to bear means to carry, so the hen letters hold the weight letter

parts.note: a laying hen is called a layer

explanation.surface: A short note telling a hen to carry some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief is British slang for a lawyer, usually a barrister handed a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is informal British usage for a legal representative who takes a case.

clue.text: Hard worker turning in too many drafts

indicators.note: turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer's letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diligent writer churns out one version after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left out 'in', which is the signal that the letters sit inside the phrase; the answer is read backwards within too many drafts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a person of tireless energy, figuratively like an electricity generator.

clue.text: Acclaimed director receives Oscar for finishing touches to The Battle of Britain

indicators.note: receives says the director's name takes in a new letter
for says the new letter stands in place of the named ones

parts.note: Ang Lee is the Oscar-winning Taiwanese film director

indicators.note: finishing touches to picks the last letter of each of the following words

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A celebrated filmmaker wins an Oscar for polishing a war film about 1940.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of The and Battle, E and E, are swapped in Ang Lee's name for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo- is a prefix meaning English or British, so it describes things of Britain.

clue.text: Maybe Stubbs composition of fair day is daring

parts.note: Una Stubbs, the English actress, is an example of an Una

indicators.note: composition of says the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The painter George Stubbs might have composed a picture of a fair day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests George Stubbs, the horse painter, but the Stubbs needed is Una Stubbs, an actress known from British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unafraid means having no fear, so a daring person is unafraid.

clue.text: Furious buccaneer losing power

indicators.note: losing means the letter for power is dropped from the word

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A sea robber becomes enraged at losing control.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Male flaps when cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter of the flaps word round to the front

parts.note: tags are small flaps or loose pieces attached to something

explanation.surface: A man panics while riding his bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is the male of a deer.

clue.text: Cleaner trained to embrace advanced living

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day

indicators.note: to embrace means the bred letters wrap around the letter for advanced

parts.note: bred can mean brought up or trained

explanation.surface: A domestic help was coached to welcome progress in life.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaning lady who comes in every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily bread is an idiom for one's livelihood, from the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Encourage noble dame working answer out

indicators.note: working means the letters are set to work in a new arrangement
out says the letter for answer is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Urging a titled lady to get the solution sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NOBLE DAME with A taken out (NOBLEDME) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To embolden someone is to give them courage, which is to encourage them.

clue.text: Desert that woman? I should think so

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to abandon a woman and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather! is an old-fashioned British exclamation of emphatic agreement, meaning certainly.
